says: In next/, the door law Q9/Q12's door-store clause compares only the Connection object's unsent and measurements tables around each refused send, while 0143 bounds every table: no span, unsent, measurement or archive row and no held object grows per refusal. A refusal that wrote a row to the door's spans, content, archived, sizes or gateway tables would leave the law green. The Project and Process stores are already compared table by table, so the door store can be compared the same way, with sums set aside.
proof: The clause at runtime-recovery.laws.integration.test.ts:1969-1972 reads only unsent and measurements from counts(door.db); .decisions/0143-a-refused-write-is-counted-never-a-row.md says no span, measurement, unsent or archive row and no held object grows per refusal. The tests step's scratch copy that compared every door table changed only unsent and measurements on the real code (field/runs/2026-11-15-t404-door-count-tests1.json), so a full comparison is green today.
cost: A future change that keeps a refused call's span in the door's spans or archived table, or writes a size row per refusal, would land green against 0143's bound.
